app.title: METASPEQ Haridra NIR — NIR Quality Analysis
app.summary: The person picks how many PLS latent variables to use and how to preprocess the spectra. Every metric and chart then recomputes with sample-wise cross-validation, and a coloured verdict rates the model's usefulness from its RPD. They pick a measured spectrum from the study, choosing a sample and one of its replicate scans, or upload a 256-point absorbance CSV. They get a predicted concentration with a green, amber or red confidence zone, set by how close it is to the calibration range. They can also overlay spectra by concentration level before and after preprocessing, check model diagnostics (predicted against reference, error against number of components, residuals), review a second assay's linearity and error at each level, and download the model card as JSON.

task.text: Build and check a multivariate calibration that predicts an analyte's concentration from a near-infrared spectrum, and flag predictions that fall outside the range the model can support.

data.text: Near-infrared absorbance spectra on a fixed wavelength grid. Each spectrum belongs to a physical sample that has several replicate scans and a reference concentration made by weighing. A second table pairs reference and predicted values for an assay at several levels.
data.item: an absorbance spectrum (one replicate scan of one blended sample) with its reference concentration

stage.text: developing and checking a spectroscopic calibration, then screening new samples against it

mechanism.text: Sidebar controls for the number of components and the preprocessing drive everything: the headline metrics, the RPD verdict and every tab are recomputed under leave-one-sample-out cross-validation. Tabs separate prediction for one spectrum (with a confidence zone and the spectrum plotted with the model band shaded), a spectral overlay, diagnostic plots with a metrics table, a second assay's linearity, and the model card with its download.

field.text: PLS calibration of NIR spectra for herbal-extract quality control in analytical chemistry

workflow.name: predict a quantity from a measurement with a validated calibration and flag when to trust it

steps.step: set up the model that will compute the result
steps.here: A slider sets the number of PLS latent variables (1–14) and a select box sets the preprocessing. Below 6 components, a warning says the model underfits.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Leave-one-sample-out cross-validation gives R², RMSECV, bias, RPD and the calibration range. A coloured banner turns the RPD into a statement of what the model is fit for.

The diagnostics show predicted against reference with an identity line and a fitted line, RMSECV against the number of latent variables with the chosen value marked, residuals against concentration with a ±SEP band, and a table of metrics.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Spectra at a chosen number of concentration levels are overlaid, shaded by level. A toggle switches between raw absorbance and preprocessed spectra cut to the model band.
Pick a study sample and one of its replicate scans, or upload a headerless CSV of 256 absorbance values. A file of any other length is rejected.

steps.step: decide whether a result can be used
steps.here: The prediction gets a GREEN, AMBER or RED confidence zone by its distance from the calibration range, measured in RMSECV. For study samples, the reference value and the difference from it are shown too.
The model card (provenance, metrics and limitations) is shown as JSON and can be downloaded, beside a written statement of scope and limitations.

distinctive: Cross-validation holds out all replicate scans of a physical sample together, so the model is always scored on a sample it has not seen.
Predictions get a three-colour confidence zone measured against the calibration range ± one RMSECV. A red prediction is extrapolation and should not be reported.
RPD is turned into a statement of fitness for use (screening, QC, release), shown as a coloured banner.
The number of components is chosen at the elbow of an RMSECV curve, with the current choice marked on it.
A second assay's absolute error is shown at each level against SEP, and from it the app sets a working range below which no number should be reported.
